title: Cross-region hardware variance mitigation and dynamic fallback matrix
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: We observe region-specific latency and tail variance for the same model+variant when served on different cloud regions and GPU SKUs (notably A100/H100/L40S/MI300). This causes: occasional SLO violations, inconsistent per-token cost estimations, and manual rollback operations during rollouts.

Goal: Define and implement a deterministic, publishable hardware-variant compatibility matrix and a runtime dynamic-fallback policy that is region-aware. The matrix will list for each model version which hardware SKUs and region combinations are certified, plus a graded compatibility score and conservative fallback variant. The runtime policy will use the matrix plus live telemetry to decide safe fallbacks (e.g., fallback to quantized variant, lower batch size, or alternative model family) without human intervention for transient variance.

Scope:
- Author schema for the compatibility matrix (CSV/JSON lines) and signing/publishing flow so Console and Dedicated control planes can consume it.
- Implement a small service that evaluates region+sku health using recent telemetry and recommends automatic temporary overrides.
- Integrate with rollout engine to prefer region-safe variants during canaries and to execute automated fallback during SLO breaches.
- Provide publishing and rollback playbooks for Model Onboarding owners and SREs.

Out of scope: model retraining or changes to model weights. This is purely serving/runtime and metadata-driven.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix schema documented and checked into //docs/model-onboarding/compat-matrix.md
Signed compatibility manifests published to artifact registry and available via API endpoint
Runtime evaluator service can compute per-region compatibility score and return a recommended fallback variant (unit + integration tests)
Rollout engine respects region-level compatibility during canary (no canary in regions with score < 0.6 unless forced)
Automated fallback triggers during synthetic SLO breach reproduceable in staging and rollouts in prod with safe circuit-breaker
Telemetry shows reduction in manual rollback incidents in the 14-day post-rollout window for new model onboardings in test cohort
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Merely publish matrix and add Console visibility (week 1). Phase 2: Staging evaluator + integration tests with canary engine (week 2). Phase 3: Gradual opt-in for <10% of new onboardings and observe (week 3). Phase 4: Enforce for all rollouts + automated fallback (week 4). Emergency rollback path and manual override documented in playbook.
test_plan: Unit tests for matrix parser and score calculator
Integration test: simulated telemetry (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) feeding evaluator, expect fallback to be suggested
End-to-end test: create canary rollout in staging with artificially lowered region score, confirm canary avoids region
Chaos test: induce tail latency spikes in one region; confirm automated fallback executes and traffic shifts without human intervention
telemetry_metrics: per-region 99th token latency delta (baseline vs. current)
per-variant per-region QPS and error rate
manual rollback count and mean time to rollback
cost-per-token drift after fallback vs pre-fallback
